faq.q: How does an assembly line work?
faq.a: The product moves along a conveyor past a series of stations, and at each one workers or robots do one task. Henry Ford's moving assembly line of 1913 showed that breaking work into small repeated steps makes building fast and consistent.

faq.q: What do robots do in a car factory?
faq.a: They do heavy, repetitive and precise jobs: welding the body, painting, lifting heavy parts, applying glue and sealant, and fitting windscreens.
asks: Why are robots used in car factories?

faq.a: A cobot, or collaborative robot, is a robot designed to work right next to people. It moves gently and has sensors that make it stop if it touches someone.

faq.q: Why do people still work on assembly lines?
faq.a: Jobs like routing wires, fitting trim and judging quality need flexible fingers and judgement that robots still struggle with. People and robots each do what they are best at.
asks: Will robots replace all factory workers?

faq.q: How long does it take to build a car?
faq.a: It depends on the factory, but a car may spend a day or more travelling through all the stations, while a finished car rolls off the end of the line every minute or so.
asks: How many cars does a factory make a day?

facts: Henry Ford introduced the moving assembly line for the Model T in 1913.

quiz.say: Why are robots used to weld car bodies?
quiz.show: Robots weld car bodies because they…

options.show: Repeat thousands of precise welds tirelessly
options.say: Repeat thousands of precise welds tirelessly

quiz.why: Welding a body means thousands of identical, precise welds, which robots do quickly and consistently.

wrong.1: Welding is repetitive and precise, not creative.
wrong.2: Robots can work around the clock, not only at night.
